## Overview

Fixes #63162: honor the tri-state `return_tokens_as_token_ids` override on both disaggregated derender paths, including generate streaming after merged #63103.

## Claims

- Explicit request true/false overrides the answering server's flag; omitted/null falls back to that server's setting.
- `/render` omits the new context key when null, preserving legacy generate compatibility for default requests. Explicit overrides require an upgraded generate node.
- Full and streaming chat/completion logprobs retain their existing placeholder-byte, decoding and hidden-reasoning contracts; raw tokens and non-derender text behavior remain unchanged.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Six new streaming cases with main's serving implementation, keeping the new context field constant | 2 failed / 4 passed before the tokenizer fix; all 6 pass after |
| Incorrect text-only `text_mode` merge negative control | All 6 fail with an error stream |
| Focused protocol, conversion and generation-stream suites, including new cases | 120 passed in 44.77s |
| Full/stream derender routes and render omission cases over HTTP | 34 passed in 82.14s |
| Contributed real-model test using the existing indirect server/client fixtures, Qwen3-0.6B | 2 passed in 102.39s |
| Additional real-model streaming parity probe, both server flags and all request values | 2 passed in 77.93s |
| All applicable pre-commit hooks, including mypy and Buildkite tethering | Passed |

The Rust frontend capability check skips the two unsupported render cases. No Rust server E2E, model-quality evaluation or performance benchmark is claimed. Existing entrypoints integration CI selects the changed suites; upstream CI has not run because the contributor pre-run gate remains unsatisfied.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands and before/after output</summary>

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_generate_stream.py \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_generate_logprobs_conversion.py \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_protocol.py \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_tokens_logprobs.py -q
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/render/test_render.py \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender.py \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py \
  -k 'logprob_override or test_render_omits_null_token_id_override' -q
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_serving_tokens.py \
  -k test_derender_logprob_request_override -q
.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run
```

For the isolated streaming regression, keep the new tests/protocol field and substitute main `3b6eeb0606`'s `serving.py`, then run:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_generate_stream.py \
  -k test_stream_derender_logprob_request_override -q
```

Before:

```text
E AssertionError: assert ('token_id:10', None) == ('é', [195, 169])
2 failed, 4 passed, 60 deselected, 1 warning in 3.49s
```

After restoring the fix:

```text
6 passed, 60 deselected, 1 warning in 3.77s
```

GPU validation used the official CUDA wheel for `7ff608a03c` (merged #63103), with the six patched Python modules overlaid and hash-matched to this rebased checkout. Serving/model Python paths are unchanged between that wheel base and the rebase base; unrelated newer Kimi kernel CMake pins were not rebuilt or validated. The Qwen checkpoint is revision `c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca`, tested on one RTX 4090 with eager execution, prefix caching disabled and 30% GPU memory utilization.

</details>

The human submitter confirmed line-by-line review of this rebased revision and personally running both the new streaming regression and the updated GPU fixture regression before publication.

## Details

The request override was dropped at render serialization, generate used only its server flag, and separate derender always decoded. A nullable `ParseContext` field preserves explicit false; field-level null omission prevents adding an unknown key for older generate nodes. Each answering path resolves the override against its own server default. Placeholder formatting reuses the existing helper; decoded logprobs retain the existing decoder and UTF-8 fallback repair.

The rebase keeps main's streaming processor setup, `_logprob_settings` and `text_mode` behavior. The model regression reuses the module's indirect server fixture, avoiding a nested server while another fixture owns GPU memory. Its Rust capability skip matches the unsupported `/render` route.

Duplicate searches found only this PR and merged #60082/#63103; neither merged feature includes this request-override fix. The affected logprobs docs explain precedence and rolling upgrade behavior. AI assistance was used for implementation, tests, documentation and review preparation.

---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

@hickeyma Addressed in 08b40a0a9593b2545ba85eb496ddd08861afe7ae.

Thanks for the detailed review. I removed the standalone route-test application and reused the existing conversion, derender and streaming suites. The real-model request-override regression now lives in `test_serving_tokens.py`, with a comment explaining the existing coupled/derender placeholder-bytes difference. The unrelated streaming rejection, hidden-reasoning, missing-context and top-count checks are gone; server defaults are passed through parametrized server fixtures without shared-state mutation.

I also removed the unused `to_chat_request()` propagation and redundant U+FFFD guards, and resolve the flag once per call beside `top_limit` on all five derender paths.

The model regression now uses the existing indirect module server/client fixtures with Qwen3-0.6B, plus the Rust frontend capability skip. Added six scripted-engine streaming override cases to `test_generate_stream.py`. With main's serving implementation and the context field held constant, the two explicit override cases fail; all six pass with the fix. The incorrect text-only merge also makes all six cases fail.

Validation: 120 focused tests, 34 HTTP cases, both contributed real-model fixture cases, two additional real-model streaming parity cases, and all applicable pre-commit checks pass. The Rust selection check skips the two unsupported cases; no Rust E2E is claimed.

@hickeyma Addressed in 638fbfd96e. Sampled and top-candidate `logprob` values now use `pytest.approx`; token strings, bytes and the rest of the response structure still compare exactly.

Validated the actual test coroutine with one-ULP differences and negative token/bytes/logprob mutations; six streaming cases and applicable pre-commit checks pass. This revision only changes test assertions; no new GPU run is claimed.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Copilot was unable to review this pull request because the user who requested the review has reached their quota limit.

Thanks @MuonChaser for pushing the fix. It looks good and covers everything in #63162. A few things to address:

- `test_render_generate_logprob_override` asserts that derender with `stream=true` returns a 400. #63103 removes that restriction, so this test breaks once that merges. It's not related to this bug anyway, so please drop it.
- There seems like a lot of tests compared to the fix. Can you move the coverage into the existing suites instead of adding a new file with its own tokenizer, engine and app?
  - `_resolve_logprobs` placeholders → `test_generate_logprobs_conversion.py`
  - `/derender` precedence → `test_derender.py` / `test_derender_stream.py`
  - `_logprobs_tokenizer` precedence → `test_serving_tokens.py` (`_build_serving_tokens` already takes the flag)
- Also drop the cases that pass whatever the flag is set to: the hidden reasoning ones, the missing `parse_context check` and the top-logprob count.
- Both tests change settings on the module scoped `app` fixture and the two derenderer references point at the same object. That only works because every test sets both values. Please use `monkeypatch` or a functionscoped fixture
- `ParseContext.to_chat_request()` now passes `return_tokens_as_token_ids` through but nothing reads it from there. Either drop it or have `_logprobs_tokenizer `read it from `derender_request` so there's one place to look.
- In `_resolve_logprobs` the `not return_tokens_as_token_ids` and checks before the U+FFFD repair can't trigger because a `token_id:N` string never ends in U+FFFD. You can remove them.
- `self._return_tokens_as_token_ids(...)` gets called for every choice. Work it out once next to `top_limit`. That'll also shorten the five call sites.
- Placeholder `bytes` come back as `null` on both derender paths. Coupled chat returns bytes there, though it's not consistent about it either. I'm fine with `null` since that matches generate's text mode but please add a comment in the parity test saying why the coupled bytes get blanked out. Right now it looks like the test is just hiding the difference.

Thanks @MuonChaser,  LGTM.

A few optional follow ups, none of them blocking:

- The new test in `test_serving_tokens.py` starts its own server for each flag value. The module `server` fixture already takes indirect params, so it could reuse that and cut most of the extra args. (My earlier pointer to `_build_serving_tokens` was wrong, sorry about that. That helper is in `test_generate_stream.py`.)
- `/render` now always sends `return_tokens_as_token_ids` in `parse_context`, even when it's null. That means an older generate node rejects every derender request, not just the ones that set it. The docs cover upgrade order but leaving the field out when it's `None` would avoid the problem.
- The streaming override test starts 6 render servers. Chat and completion could share one per flag value.

🔴 During a render-first rolling upgrade, every `output_mode: "derender"` request fails with a 400 on older generate nodes, including requests that never set the flag. The new `return_tokens_as_token_ids` field defaults to `None`, but `/render` always serializes it. Older nodes reject any unknown `parse_context` key in derender mode, including a null value. Fix: omit the field from the `/render` output when it is `None`, for example by building ParseContext with only the explicitly set value. Only requests that actually set the override should then need an upgraded generate node.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

ServingRender._build_parse_context (vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/render/serving.py:236) always sets `return_tokens_as_token_ids=request.return_tokens_as_token_ids`, which is usually `None`. The `/render` routes return the whole GenerateRequest through `create_json_response` (render/api_router.py:50, :71), so `"return_tokens_as_token_ids": null` appears in every `parse_context`. Older generate nodes parse ParseContext with `extra="allow"`. Their `_check_parse_context_fields` (protocol.py:403) then fails any derender request that has an unknown key. As a result, every derender request routed from an upgraded render node to an older generate node gets a 400, not just ones that use the new override. On the base branch the field is absent and these requests succeed. The doc note in token_in_token_out.md says to upgrade generate nodes first and calls this accepted. It still means a render-first or mixed rollout breaks all derender traffic, and omitting the field when it is null would avoid that cost.

**Verification:** Trigger: render nodes are upgraded before generate nodes, and clients send `output_mode: "derender"`. render/serving.py:236 always sets `return_tokens_as_token_ids`, so every parse_context carries `"return_tokens_as_token_ids": null`. `_check_parse_context_fields` (base protocol.py:402-411) raises, and that becomes a 400. Before this change those requests worked.

</details>

nodes.body:
@MuonChaser #63103 merged and this needs a rebase. Some things to be handled also:

- In `serving.py`, keep main's side and just pass `request` to `_logprobs_tokenizer`. The PR's `text_mode` line breaks streaming derender logprobs.
- `test_derender_logprob_request_override` needs the Rust frontend skip because `/render` returns 501 there. It should also use the indirect `server` param becaue a second server will probably fail the free memory check while the module server holds the GPU. I said this was optional last time but it's required now.
- Please add a mock test in `test_generate_stream.py` for the override with `stream: true`.

Thanks @MuonChaser nearly there. One more change:

`test_derender_logprob_request_override` compares logprobs with `==` across separate requests. Exact floats could make this flaky. The server fixture's comment already mentions 1 ULP differences on ROCm and `test_derender_parity.py` only compares `token` and `bytes`. Please compare `token` and `bytes` exactly and use `pytest.approx` for `logprob`.

Thanks @MuonChaser for the update. One last thing. The default `pytest.approx` tolerance is too tight here. With a bf16 model, a one step logit change moves the logprob by much more than `1e-6` relative and near certain tokens round to steps of about `1.2e-7`. The default `abs=1e-12` won't absorb this. Do you mind using `pytest.approx(x, abs=1e-3)` as `test_vision.py` does?

files.patch:
@@ -124,6 +124,8 @@ The server keeps no state between calls. Everything the next call needs is in `s
 
 `/inference/v1/generate` returns `GenerateLogProbs` with integer `token_id`s (the generate server has no tokenizer), and derender turns those into `ChatCompletionLogProbs` / `CompletionLogProbs`, filling `token` and `bytes` from the tokenizer with the usual U+FFFD byte-fallback correction. Generate returns every top-k candidate the engine produced; derender keeps the ones the coupled endpoint would, with the same helpers: the first `top_logprobs` on chat (all of them for `top_logprobs=-1`) and the first `logprobs + 1` on completions (all of them for `logprobs=-1`). It reads those values from `chat_request` / `completion_request`, so without the original request, or with one that does not ask for logprobs, it returns every candidate. Requests that use `logprob_token_ids` get no output logprobs from generate (their `sampling_params.logprobs` is unset), so derender has none to return for them either. Streaming derender does the same per chunk on both the plain detokenization path and the parser path (see [Streaming state and logprobs](#streaming-state-and-logprobs)). As on `/v1/chat/completions`, a request with `include_reasoning: false` and a parser configured gets no logprobs at all, batch or streaming, since the decoded logprob tokens would reveal the hidden reasoning.
 
+For both chat and completion derender, `return_tokens_as_token_ids` in `chat_request` / `completion_request` takes precedence over the answering render server's `--return-tokens-as-token-ids`. `true` returns `token_id:N` logprob tokens (`bytes: null` in the chat shape); explicit `false` returns decoded strings even when the server flag is enabled. An omitted or `null` value, or no original request, uses the render server's flag. This applies to full responses and streaming chunks, including top logprobs. It does not change decoded message content or completion text, or the suppression of logprobs when reasoning is hidden.
+
 ## Streaming cost
 
 Streaming derender threads a client carried `stream_state` across per-chunk calls instead of keeping session state on the server.

 ### Derender
 
-`derender` returns the assistant `message` a coupled `/v1/chat/completions` would, without a separate [derender](derenderer.md) call. `/v1/chat/completions/render` and `/v1/messages/render` return `parse_context` on the `GenerateRequest`. Send it back with `output_mode: "derender"`. It carries the tools, `tool_choice`, `include_reasoning`, resolved JSON only `chat_template_kwargs` and the history tool call count. A `parse_context` field this server doesn't know fails a `derender` request and is ignored at the other levels.
+`derender` returns the assistant `message` a coupled `/v1/chat/completions` would, without a separate [derender](derenderer.md) call. `/v1/chat/completions/render` and `/v1/messages/render` return `parse_context` on the `GenerateRequest`. Send it back with `output_mode: "derender"`. It carries the tools, `tool_choice`, `include_reasoning`, `return_tokens_as_token_ids`, resolved JSON only `chat_template_kwargs` and the history tool call count. A `parse_context` field this server doesn't know fails a `derender` request and is ignored at the other levels.
 
 - The parser reads the engine's `text`, so it sees the stop string cut and the post `adjust_request` decode flags. That makes it match coupled chat for parsers whose `adjust_request` changes decoding which `/derender` can't.
 - A server with a tool or reasoning parser needs `parse_context`. Without a parser, `message.content` is the plain text.
@@ -108,6 +108,10 @@ data: {"request_id": "...", "output_mode": "derender", "choices": [{"index": 0,
 
 With `output_mode: "tokens"`, logprobs are `GenerateLogProbs` with an integer `token_id` and `rank` per entry and no `token` or `bytes` (see [Generate Output Logprobs](renderer.md#generate-output-logprobs)). With `output_mode: "text"`, they are `ChatCompletionLogProbs` carrying the decoded token strings and their UTF-8 `bytes` for the sampled token and every entry in `top_logprobs`; a server started with `--return-tokens-as-token-ids` returns `token_id:N` placeholders there instead, as `/v1/completions` does.
 
+With `output_mode: "derender"`, `parse_context.return_tokens_as_token_ids` overrides the generate server's `--return-tokens-as-token-ids` when it is not `null`: `true` returns `token_id:N` placeholders with `bytes: null`, and `false` returns decoded tokens and UTF-8 bytes even when the server flag is enabled. An omitted or `null` value uses the generate server's flag. `/render` preserves explicit `true` and `false` without applying the render server's flag, and omits the context field when the request value is omitted or `null`. This setting affects logprobs only; the assistant message is still parsed from text.
+

Requests with an omitted or `null` override remain compatible because `/render` leaves that field out. Unknown parse-context fields remain ignored in `tokens` and `text` modes.

inline_comments.body:
🔴 During a render-first rolling upgrade, every `output_mode: "derender"` request fails with a 400 on older generate nodes, including requests that never set the flag. The new `return_tokens_as_token_ids` field defaults to `None`, but `/render` always serializes it. Older nodes reject any unknown `parse_context` key in derender mode, including a null value. Fix: omit the field from the `/render` output when it is `None`, for example by building ParseContext with only the explicitly set value. Only requests that actually set the override should then need an upgraded generate node.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

ServingRender._build_parse_context (vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/render/serving.py:236) always sets `return_tokens_as_token_ids=request.return_tokens_as_token_ids`, which is usually `None`. The `/render` routes return the whole GenerateRequest through `create_json_response` (render/api_router.py:50, :71), so `"return_tokens_as_token_ids": null` appears in every `parse_context`. Older generate nodes parse ParseContext with `extra="allow"`. Their `_check_parse_context_fields` (protocol.py:403) then fails any derender request that has an unknown key. As a result, every derender request routed from an upgraded render node to an older generate node gets a 400, not just ones that use the new override. On the base branch the field is absent and these requests succeed. The doc note in token_in_token_out.md says to upgrade generate nodes first and calls this accepted. It still means a render-first or mixed rollout breaks all derender traffic, and omitting the field when it is null would avoid that cost.

**Verification:** Trigger: render nodes are upgraded before generate nodes, and clients send `output_mode: "derender"`. render/serving.py:236 always sets `return_tokens_as_token_ids`, so every parse_context carries `"return_tokens_as_token_ids": null`. `_check_parse_context_fields` (base protocol.py:402-411) raises, and that becomes a 400. Before this change those requests worked.

</details>

Addressed in 4084e72cfd.

Fixed by omitting only `None` at the `ParseContext` field's serialization boundary. Missing/null request values no longer add a key to `/render` responses; explicit false and true remain serialized and retain their precedence.

The new live render-server regression fails for the two default cases before the change and passes all four cases after it. I also checked the actual HTTP payloads against the generate protocol from b689feb9f2: default requests are accepted, while explicit overrides still fail closed in derender mode. The broader routes (34 tests), focused suites (101 tests), real-model regression (2 tests) and staged pre-commit checks pass. Updated the rollout documentation accordingly.

@hickeyma Addressed in 08b40a0a9593b2545ba85eb496ddd08861afe7ae.

Thanks for the detailed review. I removed the standalone route-test application and reused the existing conversion, derender and streaming suites. The real-model request-override regression now lives in `test_serving_tokens.py`, with a comment explaining the existing coupled/derender placeholder-bytes difference. The unrelated streaming rejection, hidden-reasoning, missing-context and top-count checks are gone; server defaults are passed through parametrized server fixtures without shared-state mutation.

I also removed the unused `to_chat_request()` propagation and redundant U+FFFD guards, and resolve the flag once per call beside `top_limit` on all five derender paths.

Validation: five representative new HTTP cases fail on the baseline for decoded-versus-placeholder mismatches; all 30 revised HTTP cases pass with the fix. The existing focused suites pass 101 tests, the real-model regression passes both server configurations, and staged pre-commit checks pass.

This pull request has merge conflicts that must be resolved before it can be
merged. Please rebase the PR, @MuonChaser.

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork

@hickeyma Addressed in a0e3dde954; rebased with #63103 included.

I kept main's streaming setup and `_logprob_settings` unchanged, including treating derender as text mode, and only passed the request into the tokenizer selector.

The model regression now uses the existing indirect module server/client fixtures with Qwen3-0.6B, plus the Rust frontend capability skip. Added six scripted-engine streaming override cases to `test_generate_stream.py`. With main's serving implementation and the context field held constant, the two explicit override cases fail; all six pass with the fix. The incorrect text-only merge also makes all six cases fail.

Validation: 120 focused tests, 34 HTTP cases, both contributed real-model fixture cases, two additional real-model streaming parity cases, and all applicable pre-commit checks pass. The Rust selection check skips the two unsupported cases; no Rust E2E is claimed.

@hickeyma Addressed in 638fbfd96e. Sampled and top-candidate `logprob` values now use `pytest.approx`; token strings, bytes and the rest of the response structure still compare exactly.

Validated the actual test coroutine with one-ULP differences and negative token/bytes/logprob mutations; six streaming cases and applicable pre-commit checks pass. This revision only changes test assertions; no new GPU run is claimed.

Thanks @MuonChaser for pushing the fix. It looks good and covers everything in #63162. A few things to address:

- `test_render_generate_logprob_override` asserts that derender with `stream=true` returns a 400. #63103 removes that restriction, so this test breaks once that merges. It's not related to this bug anyway, so please drop it.
- There seems like a lot of tests compared to the fix. Can you move the coverage into the existing suites instead of adding a new file with its own tokenizer, engine and app?
  - `_resolve_logprobs` placeholders → `test_generate_logprobs_conversion.py`
  - `/derender` precedence → `test_derender.py` / `test_derender_stream.py`
  - `_logprobs_tokenizer` precedence → `test_serving_tokens.py` (`_build_serving_tokens` already takes the flag)
- Also drop the cases that pass whatever the flag is set to: the hidden reasoning ones, the missing `parse_context check` and the top-logprob count.
- Both tests change settings on the module scoped `app` fixture and the two derenderer references point at the same object. That only works because every test sets both values. Please use `monkeypatch` or a functionscoped fixture
- `ParseContext.to_chat_request()` now passes `return_tokens_as_token_ids` through but nothing reads it from there. Either drop it or have `_logprobs_tokenizer `read it from `derender_request` so there's one place to look.
- In `_resolve_logprobs` the `not return_tokens_as_token_ids` and checks before the U+FFFD repair can't trigger because a `token_id:N` string never ends in U+FFFD. You can remove them.
- `self._return_tokens_as_token_ids(...)` gets called for every choice. Work it out once next to `top_limit`. That'll also shorten the five call sites.
- Placeholder `bytes` come back as `null` on both derender paths. Coupled chat returns bytes there, though it's not consistent about it either. I'm fine with `null` since that matches generate's text mode but please add a comment in the parity test saying why the coupled bytes get blanked out. Right now it looks like the test is just hiding the difference.

Thanks @MuonChaser,  LGTM.

A few optional follow ups, none of them blocking:

- The new test in `test_serving_tokens.py` starts its own server for each flag value. The module `server` fixture already takes indirect params, so it could reuse that and cut most of the extra args. (My earlier pointer to `_build_serving_tokens` was wrong, sorry about that. That helper is in `test_generate_stream.py`.)
- `/render` now always sends `return_tokens_as_token_ids` in `parse_context`, even when it's null. That means an older generate node rejects every derender request, not just the ones that set it. The docs cover upgrade order but leaving the field out when it's `None` would avoid the problem.
- The streaming override test starts 6 render servers. Chat and completion could share one per flag value.

@MuonChaser #63103 merged and this needs a rebase. Some things to be handled also:

- In `serving.py`, keep main's side and just pass `request` to `_logprobs_tokenizer`. The PR's `text_mode` line breaks streaming derender logprobs.
- `test_derender_logprob_request_override` needs the Rust frontend skip because `/render` returns 501 there. It should also use the indirect `server` param becaue a second server will probably fail the free memory check while the module server holds the GPU. I said this was optional last time but it's required now.
- Please add a mock test in `test_generate_stream.py` for the override with `stream: true`.

Thanks @MuonChaser nearly there. One more change:

`test_derender_logprob_request_override` compares logprobs with `==` across separate requests. Exact floats could make this flaky. The server fixture's comment already mentions 1 ULP differences on ROCm and `test_derender_parity.py` only compares `token` and `bytes`. Please compare `token` and `bytes` exactly and use `pytest.approx` for `logprob`.

Thanks @MuonChaser for the update. One last thing. The default `pytest.approx` tolerance is too tight here. With a bf16 model, a one step logit change moves the logprob by much more than `1e-6` relative and near certain tokens round to steps of about `1.2e-7`. The default `abs=1e-12` won't absorb this. Do you mind using `pytest.approx(x, abs=1e-3)` as `test_vision.py` does?
